eli5.text: The coding assistant you use just received a routine behind-the-scenes update that keeps your installation current. This version bump itself only changes a number; no new features or fixes are visible to you right now. Behind the scenes, this release packages a set of related changes, the most user-affecting being that error messages now include the raw original error details, error logging has been made more consistent, and analytics reporting has been restructured. If you update to this version, you get all of those improvements together; otherwise, nothing you see changes today.

ai.title: Add shared analytics dispatcher for CLI and Web loggers
ai.summary: Introduces createAnalyticsDispatcher in common/src/util/analytics-dispatcher.ts to centralize event routing, dev gating, and buffering. CLI and Web loggers replace manual analyticsBuffer logic with this shared utility, calling dispatcher.process() to retrieve payloads for trackEvent. The new module handles flush-on-userId resolution and returns empty arrays in dev environments.

eli5.text: When you use the CodeBuff CLI or web tool, your errors and events are now collected by a single shared helper that decides when to actually send them out. This helper waits to group related errors together until it knows which user you are (or your account id), and it makes sure nothing leaks out during local development. As a result, your error reports should be more consistent between the command-line and web versions, and developers won't see random test errors appear as real analytics data.

ai.title: Refine shared analytics logging and error handling
ai.summary: Centralizes analytics payload construction in `common/src/util/analytics-log.ts` and adds structured error logging to `cli/src/utils/analytics.ts` via `setAnalyticsErrorLogger`. The CLI logger now delegates event ID extraction and user ID resolution to shared helpers, while the Web logger adopts the same payload generation for production tracking. This reduces duplication and ensures consistent PostHog event formatting across surfaces.

eli5.text: When the assistant logs what it's doing, it now builds that logging information in one shared spot and sends clearer, more consistent details to PostHog (the analytics service). If you're watching logs in real time, you won't notice a difference; behind the scenes, errors that happen while tracking usage are now caught and reported with more context, so issues are easier to diagnose without breaking your session. This affects anyone running the CLI or using the web version today.

This change impacts CLI analytics/logging, SDK constants, Web logger, Evals logger, and BigQuery client. `sdk/src/constants.ts` now re-exports these flags, while `IS_CI` is derived from `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS`.

eli5.text: The CLI tool now uses simple yes/no switches like IS_DEV, IS_TEST, IS_PROD, and IS_CI to decide whether to send usage analytics and write logs, instead of checking the environment string directly each time. This affects the CLI's analytics and logging behavior, as well as the web logger, SDK constants, and BigQuery client, they all now rely on these shared switches. To you, nothing looks different, but behind the scenes the code that decides what gets tracked and logged is now cleaner and more consistent across all parts of the application.

ai.title: Remove speed pressure from thinker selector prompt
ai.summary: The `thinker-selector.ts` prompt no longer instructs the model to minimize word count or skip `<think>` tags for obvious cases. This change removes the dual goal of speed and quality, allowing the selector to use full reasoning when distinguishing between similar thinking outputs. Scope is limited to the internal best-of-n selection logic in `.agents/thinker/best-of-n/`.

eli5.text: The internal system that picks which batch of reasoning to keep now has more time to think it over. You won't notice this directly since it's behind-the-scenes logic, but the selector is no longer told to rush by skipping its usual step-by-step thinking, so it can take its time when comparing similar outputs. This is live today in the best-of-n selection path.

ai.title: Add git checkout warning to knowledge.md
ai.summary: Added 'Preserving Uncommitted Changes' section to knowledge.md. Warns against using git checkout HEAD -- or git restore to exclude files from commits, as this destructively discards uncommitted work. Recommends only git add the specific files to include. Scope: Internal documentation guidelines.

eli5.text: A warning was added to the internal documentation telling developers never to use git checkout or git restore to remove files from a commit, since doing so permanently deletes any unsaved work. This affects internal developers who manage code changes using git, and if they looked at the documentation they would now see a new section called 'Preserving Uncommitted Changes' with clear instructions to instead only add the specific files they want to include in a commit.
